- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.1), model often misjudges mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward correction after sentiment dips below 0.2.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment’s lack of momentum.
